_comment: NORMATIVE cross-language fixtures for the Techee pairing ceremony.
The safety number is what matters most here: two humans compare it out of band, so
if Android and Windows compute it differently, pairing fails visibly and
unfixably for the user. It is pinned below and asserted in all three languages.
IMPORTANT - the two proof transcripts are RAW CONCATENATIONS with no domain
separator and no length framing. That is not how the rest of Techee builds signed
input, and it is a known weakness (see docs/PROTOCOL.md section 2.3). It is
reproduced exactly because it is what the shipped Android app does; an endpoint
that framed them differently could not pair with any existing phone. The
concatenation is unambiguous ONLY because every field is fixed-length, so
implementations MUST enforce those lengths rather than assume them.
All keypairs below are throwaways generated solely for this file.

lengths._note: P-256 SPKI DER is always 91 bytes. The unframed proof transcripts depend on this; verify it, do not trust it.

ecdh._rule: Raw ECDH shared secret = the X coordinate, UNHASHED. Android uses KeyAgreement.generateSecret() which returns exactly this; .NET must use DeriveRawSecretAgreement (NOT DeriveKeyMaterial, which hashes). Applying a KDF here changes the safety number and breaks pairing.

safetyNumber._rule: sha256(shared || min(pubA,pubB) || max(pubA,pubB)), ordered by the lowercase-hex rendering of each DER key; then the first 6 bytes each rendered as a zero-padded 3-digit decimal and joined by "-". 48 bits total, no domain separation - a known weakness matched deliberately for compatibility.
safetyNumber._orderIndependent: Computing it with the two identity keys swapped MUST give the same result.

host._weakness: Carries no nonce and does not cover the host own ephemeral key, so it proves possession of the host identity but contributes no freshness. The out-of-band safety number remains the real anti-MITM check.

offerJson._rule: QR payload field names, matching Android PairingManager.PairingOffer exactly.
